chunks: Abu Kahmas asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
About the first two rakʿahs: if I sit in them for the tashahhud and, while sitting, I say, “Al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuhu,” is that the ending?
He said, “No. But when you say, ‘Al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa ʿalā ʿibādi llāhi al-ṣāliḥīn,’ then that is the ending.”

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs being discussed in the prayer
key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ: the greeting addressed to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during the prayer
key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ الل: the formula identified here as constituting the ending of the prayer
key_terms.انْصِرَافٌ: the completion or ending by which one exits the prayer
key_terms.عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ: the righteous servants of Allah included in the prayer greeting
key_terms.لِلتَّشَهُّدِ: for the tashahhud, the seated testimony in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Which phrase in the tashahhud marks the ending of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the conclusion of salat (prayer) during the tashahhud. It states that saying “Al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu...” does not itself constitute the ending of the prayer, whereas saying “Al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa ʿalā ʿibādi llāhi al-ṣāliḥīn” does.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1014 - Abu Kahmas asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the two rak'ahs of prayer when, after sitting in the tashahhud position, he says:
"As-Salamu Alayka Ayyuha An-Nabi wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh"
(Peace be upon you, O’ Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings). Is this considered the ending (of the prayer)?
Imam (as) replied: "No, it is not the ending. But when you say 'As-Salamu Alayna wa Ala Ibadillah As-Saliheen' (Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah (swt)), that is the ending."
